$comment: Canonical key set for ONE row of `fno agents list --json`. Two serializers produce this shape and they have drifted before (the Rust one stayed pinned to the pre-v10 keys and dropped harness, harness_session_id and mux for every live row, so operators and agents read a fully bound pane worker as unhosted and unidentified). Both are asserted against this file: cli/src/fno/agents/format.py::serialize_entry and the `agent.list` projection in crates/fno-agents/src/daemon.rs. Adding or removing a key means editing this file first; a serializer that disagrees fails its own test.

stored.provider: The registry's spawn-stamped model vendor (v15+ axis), never inferred from `harness`. Restored to the projection by x-f273: the pre-v15 alias that carried the HARNESS value under this name was removed for lying, and that removal kept hiding the real vendor axis the rename had just created, so `fno agents list` answered null for a field the writer stored (30 of 31 live rows lost, 2026-08-22). `observed_model` remains the transcript-derived reading of what actually answered; this key answers which vendor's lane the row was minted for. Both serializers emit it or the parity asserts fail.

removed.model: OMITTED FROM THE ROW PROJECTION. Registry storage records intended model configuration, while `observed_model` is the actual transcript-derived reading. Do not expose intended configuration as though it were observed runtime truth.

derived.address: The mailbox address this row can actually receive at: `canonical_handle(harness_session_id)`, the first eight of the session id, which is the same string `fno agents mail drain-self` computes for itself. It exists because every other identifier in the row is something else. `name` is a spawn label and a name-lane durable write is the largest still-growing category of stranded mail; `handle` in the discovered lane is a friendly alias; `short_id` is a transport key that is null for most registry rows. A reader with no address column copies `name`, and that mail queues under a key nobody drains. Null when no identity was recorded - absence is reported as absence, never as a plausible-looking handle. Falls back to `short_id` for claude ONLY, where the transport key IS the first eight; a codex or opencode `short_id` is a daemon worker key and would advertise a mailbox that does not exist. Deliberately NOT promoted to the full session id on a first-eight collision: ambiguity detection already lives in the send resolver, which fails closed and names the candidates, and a second implementation here would be a second answer to one question.
derived.reachability: The one derivation with a declared basis (cli/src/fno/agents/reachability.py). `reachability` is the verdict (reachable | unreachable | unknown), `basis` is the evidence it was reached from (transcript | process-gone | pane-gone | silent | no-evidence), and `last_activity_age_s` is how old that evidence is. The three travel together on purpose: a bare verdict cannot separate a positive transcript reading from a fired falsifier, and `unknown` at 30s means something different from `unknown` at 30h. `status` keeps the older wire vocabulary its consumers already parse, and says WHAT the row is; the triple says which question was answered. Both serializers read it from the same `fno agents truth --json` probe - the Rust one from the probe it already ran for `status` - so they cannot disagree about the same row. All three are null when the probe did not answer, which is not the same as `no-evidence`: that is a verdict, this is an absent reading.
derived.progress: The orthogonal axis beside `reachability`, from `classify_progress` (cli/src/fno/agents/reachability.py). `reachability` answers 'can I reach this process'; `progress` answers 'is it taking its own next turn, waiting on the operator, parked, or refused' - a question reachability cannot answer, since a refused worker is fully reachable. `progress` is the verdict (advancing | awaiting-operator | parked | refused | unknown), `progress_basis` is the evidence it was reached from (transcript-turn | operator-turn | promise | model-refused | no-evidence | silent). Advancing requires a measured transcript advance inside the ten-minute evidence window; an older `working` state is unknown / silent and an unreadable activity age is unknown / no-evidence. Both null when the probe did not answer, which is an absent reading, never the `unknown` verdict.
derived.progress_basis: See `progress` above; the two travel together the same way `reachability`/`basis` do.
derived.last_event_at: The absolute ISO8601 UTC stamp of the worker's newest transcript activity, derived from the same epoch as `last_activity_age_s` in the same `fno agents truth --json` probe read, so the stamp and the age cannot disagree about one transcript. Exists because a relative age decays the instant it is read: a cached JSON blob's seconds-ago figure is already wrong by however long since the daemon computed it, while the stamp is not. Null when the probe never answered - an absent reading is reported as absence, never as a fresh event.
derived.last_message: The flattened text of the transcript's LAST turn (assistant or user - the same turn `classify_tail` reads), with claude/codex content blocks compacted (`[tool_use: name]` markers inline), whitespace collapsed, capped at 200 chars. Comes from the same truth probe as `last_event_at`. Distinct from `last_message_at`, which is registry metadata and is null on many rows while the worker is mid-sentence; a table column named LAST MESSAGE that renders a timestamp or a dash was the bug this key retires. Null when the probe never answered - never a fabricated message and never a health claim.
derived.observed_model: What the worker is ACTUALLY answering as, read from its own transcript by fno.agents.session_truth.observed_model - never from anything the spawn recorded, which reports the INTENDED model in exactly the case an operator suspects a silent fallback. A discriminated object: {kind: observed, model, samples} | {kind: no-transcript} | {kind: not-file-backed} | {kind: no-model-yet} | {kind: unreadable, reason}. The five never collapse into one unknown: no-model-yet is a worker that came up and never processed a turn, not-file-backed is a harness that keeps no per-session file at all, and neither is the same thing as a worker whose transcript has not appeared yet. Both serializers derive it from the same Python resolver (the Rust daemon shells out to `fno agents truth --json`, one probe per row, the one it already ran for `status`), so the two cannot report different models for the same worker.
derived.liveness_origin: Whether the pid on this row started with the session (`survivor`) or after it (`resumed`), from a 600 second band between `created_at` and `pid_start_time`. `liveness_origin_basis` is the evidence, and the two travel together the same way `reachability`/`basis` do: a bare null cannot separate `no pid on this row` from `a start token this parser cannot read`, and callers acted on that null as though it meant the first. Null verdict always carries a basis (pid-absent | created-at-absent | created-at-unreadable | pid-start-absent | pid-start-unreadable); a non-null verdict carries a null basis, because the value is its own evidence. Both producers derive it from one rule asserted by the shared corpus at schemas/agents-row-contradiction.json. That corpus binds the RULE, not its callers: every case supplies `pid` by hand, so a serializer that omits it reads pid-absent forever while the corpus stays green. Assert the field on the serializer too.
derived.liveness_origin_basis: See `liveness_origin` above; the two travel together.

rust_only.$comment: Keys the Rust daemon projection emits on top of `required`. A harmless superset: the Python list surface has no equivalent source field.

python_only.$comment: Keys the Python serializer emits on top of `required`. Add one only when the Rust projection genuinely CANNOT answer the same question, never because it was easier. The reachability triple was briefly listed here, which was the wrong call and is worth recording: a triple emitted Python-side only was missing from the daemon projection that the mux table and fleetview read, while peek and the daemon's own census comment both sent readers to `fno agents list` to find it. Both serializers now emit it from the same `fno agents truth --json` probe. Which serializer is reachable, measured 2026-08-20: `fno agents list` is served by the PYTHON `serialize_entry`. The Rust `fno` binary forwards every non-mux subcommand to the Python CLI, and crates/fno/src/server.rs:1205 reaches the daemon's own view by shelling back out to `agents list --json`. The daemon's `agent.list` projection answers the RPC its consumers make. Earlier revisions of this comment claimed the reverse and sent a reader building an operator-facing column toward the serializer nobody was reading. `dnd` (x-481e) meets the bar the triple did not: it is the remaining time on a busy-mode hold, read from a clock whose directory is resolved by fno's own path config (`fno.paths.state_dir()`), which the daemon does not load. The daemon emits the raw `delivery_policy` it stores, which answers 'is mail held'; `dnd` answers 'until when' and only the config-aware side can. The one operator-facing DND column is the Python table, so nothing that renders it is missing it. Four values, and a consumer must handle all four: a duration (`~4m`, `~30s`) for a timed hold; `held` for a policy with no expiry recorded; `?` when the clock could not be read, which is NOT the same as no hold and must never render as the empty cell; and null when mail is flowing despite the flag, which is the lapsed-hold case.
